05 ADHD and sleep · class card

Sleep agents

nonbenzodiazepine hypnotics (Z-drugs) · zolpidem · zaleplon · eszopiclone · ramelteon

Key point
  • Zolpidem, zaleplon and eszopiclone (the Z-drugs): act on gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) type A receptors at the benzodiazepine site faster sleep onset, with less tolerance and dependence than benzodiazepines
  • Flumazenil: reverses the Z-drugs
  • Zaleplon helps sleep onset only; zolpidem and eszopiclone (longest half-life) help onset and maintenance
  • Ramelteon, a melatonin agonist: sleep onset, few adverse effects, no dependence, safe in older adults
  • Never with alcohol or another central nervous system (CNS) depressant; in older adults, ataxia and falls
Drugs

Zolpidem Ambien: sleep onset and maintenance

Zaleplon: sleep onset only MnemonicZaleplon mnemonicZaleplON(SET): onset

Eszopiclone Lunesta: onset and maintenance; the longest half-life of the three MnemonicEszopiclone mnemonicLongest name, longest half-life

Ramelteon Rozerem: sleep onset only; not a controlled substance MnemonicRamelteon mnemonicRamelteON: onset

Mechanism

Z-drug the benzodiazepine site of GABA-A, more selective for benzodiazepine type 1 (BZ1) than benzodiazepines are shorter sleep latency; less likely to change the sleep cycle

Rapid liver metabolism short duration of action

Ramelteon melatonin receptors in the suprachiasmatic nucleus sleep onset

Uses

Insomnia that stays severe after cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I): lowest dose, shortest time

Zolpidem, brief use: situational insomnia, including the insomnia of adjustment disorder

Ramelteon: trouble falling asleep

Melatonin, acting at melatonin receptors, first; clonazepam if symptoms persist: rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder

Adverse effects

Older adults are more sensitive: cognitive impairment, headache, delirium

Older adults: central ataxia falls

See the danger rows below

Long-term use: tolerance to the hypnotic effect, somnolence, dependence, cognitive impairment, though less tolerance and dependence than benzodiazepines

On the board: no significant or amnesia In practiceNext-day impairmentIn practice: zolpidem and eszopiclone cause next-day impairment, including drivingCause: a dose that leaves too little of the night for sleepZolpidem: leave 7 to 8 hours for sleepZolpidem: 5 mg starting dose for womenZolpidem: 5 mg dose for older adults Complex sleep behaviorsBoxed warning: zolpidem, eszopicloneComplex sleep behaviors may occurExamples: sleep-walking, sleep-driving, other acts while not fully awakeStop the drug at once if one occurs

: few, nonspecific (dizziness, nausea, fatigue, headache) Ramelteon and fluvoxamineFluvoxamine: barred with ramelteon

Additive CNS depressionDeeper sedation and slowed breathing when alcohol, opioid, benzodiazepine, barbiturate or first-generation antihistamine joins a Z-drug

If an opioid or nightly alcohol is on the history, choose no Z-drug; a benzodiazepine carries the same risk.

Ataxia and falls in older adultsUnsteady gait, confusion or delirium after a bedtime dose; night falls

Diphenhydramine is no better choice: heavy sedation for questionable benefit

If an older adult needs a drug for trouble falling asleep, choose ramelteon.

OversedationHeavy sedation after a Z-drug overdose

In a long-term benzodiazepine user, the antidote can set off withdrawal and seizures

If Z-drug sedation must be reversed, choose flumazenil.

Practice
  1. 78-year-old woman with trouble falling asleep for 4 months sleeps through once asleep; cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia helped only partly uses a walker; one fall last year examination normal · no depression on screening → Ramelteon → ramelteon shortens time to sleep onset in older adults with a lower adverse-effect burden; antihistamines bring excessive sedation for little benefit, and benzodiazepines add dependence, confusion and falls
  2. 52-year-old woman wakes at 3 AM most nights and cannot fall back asleep 4 months; sleep hygiene and cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia did not help no depression, snoring or alcohol; falls asleep easily examination normal → Eszopiclone → eszopiclone, like zolpidem, helps both falling and staying asleep and has the longest half-life of the Z-drugs; zaleplon and ramelteon help sleep onset only
  3. 74-year-old woman has fallen twice at night on the way to the bathroom started zolpidem 3 weeks ago for trouble falling asleep unsteady after each bedtime dose, steady by morning orthostatic vital signs normal · reflexes and vibration sense normal → Zolpidem adverse effect → Z-drugs can cause central ataxia, and older adults are more sensitive to their adverse effects, so night falls follow a bedtime dose; normal orthostatic vital signs and a normal reflex and vibration exam argue against the other two
